Company facts, metrics and program claims are drawn from public Esyasoft material or the supplied GET travel/accommodation FAQ. Where a detail is not publicly documented, this guide does not invent an internal policy.

Esyasoft describes itself as a global energy transition technology group. Its public positioning spans smart utilities, software/analytics/AI, Energy as a Service, battery energy storage systems and e-mobility, across electricity, water and gas utilities and related energy-transition services. [S1]

For a new engineer, the important idea is that Esyasoft is not simply a software company and not simply a metering company. Its public portfolio combines physical infrastructure, connected devices, digital platforms, data, analytics, AI and energy services.
Physical world → connected infrastructure → data → software → intelligence → operational action. Esyasoft's portfolio covers multiple layers of this chain.
Smart Utility Solutions; Software, Analytics & AI; Energy as a Service; BESS; e-Mobility. [S1]
To be the world's largest energy transition company driving the future of energy. [S3]
Directly impact 1 billion lives and reduce ~10B tCO2e. [S3]
Corporate material describes activity across 12+ countries; the homepage separately uses a 10+ countries metric. [S1][S2]
Corporate metrics change over time. Treat these figures as a snapshot of the public website at the research date.

Esyasoft states that it was founded in 2014 with a vision to make energy smarter, more efficient and more accessible. Published milestones show an evolution from smart-grid and smart-metering capability toward a broader energy-transition portfolio. [S4]
First Smart Grid deployment in India under the guidance of India's Ministry of Power. [S4]
Startup Innovation Grant from the Government of Karnataka. [S4]
More than 25M connected endpoints; large AMI implementation across five UAE emirates. [S4]
Global ESG recognitions including sustainability and work-environment awards. [S4]
Graduate-program expansion and Mangalore Global Capability Development & R&D Centre. [S5][S6]
U.S. expansion, new partnerships and continued expansion of the portfolio; Correla joined the group in September. [S7][S8][S9]

Esyasoft's published vision is “To be the world's largest energy transition company driving the future of energy.” It describes achieving this through technologies, infrastructure and platforms enabling smarter, cleaner and more connected energy systems. [S3]
People are at the core of what the company does, internally and externally. [S3]
Innovation, quality products and continuous learning are emphasized. [S3]
Agility, flexibility and continuous improvement are emphasized, including technology and data to improve efficiency. [S3]
The public values point toward three habits: learn continuously, care about technical quality, and connect your work to reliable delivery and real outcomes.
Identify a physical or business problem: poor visibility, manual reading, losses, reliability issues, demand uncertainty, EV charging complexity or energy-management needs.
Connect the physical environment: meters, gateways, sensors, chargers, storage assets or other infrastructure.
Collect and move data securely through devices, gateways, protocols, networks and integrations.
Manage and contextualize data through systems such as HES, MDMS and related platforms.
Analyze and interpret through dashboards, analytics, forecasting, AI, digital twins and operational intelligence.
Act through billing, monitoring, maintenance, loss reduction, demand management, charging optimization, storage dispatch or other operational decisions.
Measure outcomes such as reliability, efficiency, visibility, cost, customer service, sustainability and resilience.
This is a conceptual onboarding model; not every deployment contains every layer.

The energy transition is the shift toward energy systems that are cleaner, more efficient, more flexible and increasingly digital. Esyasoft's material connects the transition with renewable generation, electrification, storage, e-mobility and digital intelligence across energy infrastructure. [S1][S10]
Producing electricity from sources such as thermal, hydro, solar or wind.
Moving bulk electricity over high-voltage networks.
Delivering electricity through local networks to consumers.
An organization providing and/or operating essential energy or water services.
Upgrading physical, digital and operational infrastructure to improve visibility, flexibility and performance.
Distributed Energy Resource; smaller resources closer to customers, such as solar or batteries.
Changing consumption in response to grid conditions, prices or operational needs.
Storing energy when its value is lower and using/selling it when its value is higher.

Esyasoft's Smart Utility Solutions are positioned around modernizing electricity, water and gas distribution through advanced metering, AMI, IoT connectivity, secure communications and digital platforms. [S11]

A smart-metering ecosystem adds communication, remote data collection and software-driven operations to measurement. Esyasoft describes AMI as combining smart meters, IoT devices, secure communications, scalable network management and digital platforms. [S11]
Measures consumption and can support additional functions depending on the device.
Moves meter/device data through wired or wireless networks.
Aggregates or translates data from multiple endpoints and communicates northbound.
Head End System: manages field-device communication and data acquisition.
Meter Data Management System: validates, processes and manages meter data for billing, reporting and analytics.
Turn validated data into operational insights, forecasting, loss analysis and other use cases.
Esyasoft's AMI 2.0 material describes a move beyond periodic billing reads toward richer data, edge computing, AI inference, bidirectional communications and software-defined metering. [S12][S13]
The meter is increasingly part of a distributed computing and sensing system—not merely a billing instrument.
METER → COMMUNICATION → HES → MDMS → ANALYTICS → ACTION
The exact architecture varies by project, but this mental model connects embedded systems, networking, backend services, databases, analytics and utility operations.
A meter records an energy reading.
The reading travels through the relevant communication path.
A gateway or field device may aggregate, translate or forward it.
The HES receives/manages device communication and data acquisition.
The MDMS validates and manages the data.
Analytics identify patterns, anomalies, losses or demand trends.
A utility user acts on the information—for example through billing, investigation, maintenance, planning or operational control.
Published case studies describe IoT gateways, water and energy meters, HES integration, LTE/GSM, protocol interoperability, remote disconnect/reconnect and real-time data acquisition. [S14][S15]

Esyasoft also notes Gartner recognition for its MDMS capability for seven consecutive years and a 2025 Gartner Hype Cycle recognition related to Smart Edge Metering Systems. [S16][S17]

Esyasoft describes Energy as a Service as a model supporting homes, businesses, utilities and industrial clients with renewable-energy access, energy optimization, demand flexibility and managed energy solutions. [S1]
For a new engineer, think of EaaS as moving beyond a one-time product toward an ongoing energy outcome delivered through infrastructure, software, data, services and optimization.

Esyasoft provides utility-scale BESS. Public material identifies applications including renewable integration, grid stability, frequency regulation, peak shaving, load shifting, energy arbitrage, backup/resilience and microgrids/community energy projects. [S18]
Renewable generation and demand do not always align in time.
Storage can shift energy across time.
Fast-response storage can support grid balancing and frequency regulation.
Storage can reduce peak demand and support resilience.
Storage can be coordinated with other digital energy systems.
Esyasoft's public news also documents a 2026 collaboration with Tesla related to battery energy storage deployments. [S19]

The public Graduate Program page describes a two-year program with three immersive rotations across strategic functions in energy, utilities and digital innovation, with global projects, emerging technologies, real-world challenges, mentorship and capability building. [S25]

A 2025 program announcement describes a 140+ trainee cohort and learning around smart metering, MDMS, DLMS, billing systems, IoT, AI applications in energy, carbon tracking, soft skills and personal effectiveness, plus niche learning tracks. [S26]

The Graduate Program is positioned as a bridge between academic potential and real-world energy-transition work: build domain context, develop technical capability, work on real problems, learn from experienced people, and grow into an active contributor.

Esyasoft describes its Mangalore Global Capability Centre as a state-of-the-art learning, development, research and residential centre. The company says it spans 50,000+ sq. ft. and includes training classrooms, IoT and embedded-systems labs, workshops and residential facilities. [S6]

The centre is intended to support practical learning, industry collaboration and professional growth; a company announcement also describes live grid simulation environments and recreational/community spaces. [S6][S27]
